segments.text: Lesson 14
segments.translation: 第14课

segments.text: The Butterfly Effect
segments.translation: 蝴蝶效应

segments.text: Listen to the tape then answer this question.
segments.translation: 听录音，然后回答问题。

segments.text: Why do small errors make it impossible to predict the weather system with a high degree of accuracy?
segments.translation: 为什么小误差导致无法准确预测天气系统？

segments.text: Beyond two or three days, the world's best weather forecasts are speculative,
segments.translation: 除了两三天之外，世界上最好的天气预报都是推测性的，

segments.text: and beyond six or seven they are worthless.
segments.translation: 六七岁以后，他们就一文不值了。

segments.text: The Butterfly Effect is the reason.
segments.translation: 原参考译文为：原因是蝴蝶效应。

segments.text: For small pieces of weather--
segments.translation: 对于小天气--

segments.text: and to a global forecaster, small can mean thunderstorms and blizzards--
segments.translation: 对于全球预报员来说，小可能意味着雷暴和暴风雪--

segments.text: any prediction deteriorates rapidly.
segments.translation: 任何预测都会迅速恶化。

segments.text: Errors and uncertainties multiply, cascading upward through a chain of turbulent features,
segments.translation: 错误和不确定性成倍增加，通过一系列湍流特征向上级联，

segments.text: from dust devils and squalls up to continent-size eddies that only satellites can see.
segments.translation: 从尘土飞扬到只有卫星才能看到的大陆大小的漩涡。

segments.text: The modern weather models work with a grid of points of the order of sixty miles apart,
segments.translation: 现代天气模型与相距60英里的网格点一起工作，

segments.text: and even so, some starting data has to be guessed,
segments.translation: 即便如此，必须猜测一些起始数据，

segments.text: since ground stations and satellites cannot see everywhere.
segments.translation: 因为地面站和卫星无法看到任何地方。

segments.text: But suppose the earth could be covered with sensors spaced one foot apart,
segments.translation: 但假设地球可能被间隔一英尺的传感器覆盖，

segments.text: rising at one-foot intervals all the way to the top of the atmosphere.
segments.translation: 一直以一英尺的间隔上升到大气层的顶部。

segments.text: Suppose every sensor gives perfectly accurate readings of temperature,
segments.translation: 假设每个传感器都能提供完全准确的温度读数，

segments.text: pressure, humidity, and any other quantity a meteorologist would want.
segments.translation: 压力、湿度和气象学家想要的任何其他数量。

segments.text: Precisely at noon an infinitely powerful computer takes all the data and calculates what will happen at each point
segments.translation: 准确地说，在中午，一台无限强大的计算机会获取所有数据，并计算每个点会发生什么

segments.text: The computer will still be unable to predict whether Princeton, New Jersey, will have sun or rain on a day one month away.
segments.translation: 电脑仍然无法预测新泽西州普林斯顿是否会在一个月后的一天有阳光或雨水。

segments.text: At noon the spaces between the sensors will hide fluctuations that the computer will not know about,
segments.translation: 在中午，传感器之间的空间将隐藏计算机不知道的波动，

segments.text: tiny deviations from the average.
segments.translation: 与平均值的微小偏差。

segments.text: By 12.01, those fluctuations will already have created small errors one foot away.
segments.translation: 到12.01 ，这些波动将在一英尺之外产生小错误。

segments.text: Soon the errors will have multiplied to the ten-foot scale, and so on up to the size of the globe.
segments.translation: 很快，误差将乘以10英尺的尺度，以此类推，直至地球的大小。
